assumptions: Fix known \(\beta,R>0\). The unknown objective is \(f(x)=\mu(x-m)^2/2+c\) on \(\mathbb R\), with \(\beta/2\le\mu\le\beta\), \(|m|\le R\), and unrestricted unknown \(c\in\mathbb R\). Thus these are \(\beta\)-smooth, \(\beta/2\)-strongly convex objectives with a minimizer within distance \(R\) of zero.

A deterministic algorithm knows this class and can choose any one query \(q\in\mathbb R\) before seeing the objective. Its only reply is the exact pair \((f(q),f'(q))\); it may use unlimited local arithmetic to output any \(z\in\mathbb R\). Neither the objective nor its optimal value is given.
mathematical_cores.boundary: Original deterministic one-query exercise. It is not an exact minimax constant, a many-query or randomized oracle lower bound, or a numbered exercise from the book. Unknown additive offsets are part of the stated information model. The Lean graph points to an analytic supporting result only; neither the oracle argument nor the stronger-information comparison is formalized in this packet.
mathematical_cores.difficulty_reason: For an arbitrary deterministic query, construct two admissible quadratics, match both oracle coordinates, convert the common transcript to a quantitative objective gap, and audit how the conclusion changes when the optimal value is known. This is a finite explicit adversary, not a claimed multi-query or research-level general lower bound. The level is provisional.
mathematical_cores.lean_explanation: Only the analytic quadratic adapter is formally linked. Apply the owned quadratic-regularization theorem on the real line with a constant base function, base smoothness zero, center m and regularization coefficient μ. Its conclusion supplies differentiability, curvature, gradient and the μ-Lipschitz estimate. The two-instance construction, indistinguishable replies, algorithmic lower bound and known-optimum comparison are not aligned Lean tasks here.
mathematical_cores.question: Show that every such algorithm has an input on which \(f(z)-f(m)\ge\beta R^2/64\). Construct two admissible objectives with the same first-order reply at the algorithm's query and justify why their common output must be bad on at least one of them. Then explain whether one query suffices to recover the minimizer on this same quadratic class if the exact optimal value \(f(m)\) is supplied in advance.

rubric.criterion: For an arbitrary deterministic query, constructs two distinct admissible instances with the stipulated radius and curvature bounds. Any valid construction is accepted.
Checks equality of both the value and the derivative at the query and justifies the common output from the deterministic information model.
Obtains the requested quantitative worst-case gap for every possible common output, with correct constants; a stronger bound earns full credit.
Shows how a known optimal value identifies the minimizer in one query for the stated quadratic class, including the case of zero derivative.

steps: Fix the algorithm, hence its query \(q\), and let \(s=1\) for \(q\ge0\) and \(s=-1\) otherwise. Choose centers on the opposite side of zero, \(m_F=-sR\) and \(m_C=-sR/2\). Their distances from the query are \(d_F=|q|+R\) and \(d_C=|q|+R/2\), and \(q-m_i=sd_i\) for either index \(i\). Put \(\mu_F=\beta d_C/d_F\) and \(\mu_C=\beta\). Since \(d_F/2\le d_C\le d_F\), both curvatures lie in \([\beta/2,\beta]\).

Use the unknown additive offsets to choose \[f_i(x)=\frac{\mu_i}{2}\big((x-m_i)^2-(q-m_i)^2\big).\] Their gradients are \(f_i'(x)=\mu_i(x-m_i)\). Their constant positive second derivatives verify the curvature constraints and give the unique minimizers \(m_i\), which lie within the prescribed radius. At \(q\), both values are zero and both gradients are \(s\beta d_C\). The common reply includes the function value, not just the derivative.

Since the algorithm is deterministic and has no other objective information, the identical reply produces a common output \(z\). The minimizers differ by \(R/2\). The triangle inequality implies \(\max_i|z-m_i|\ge R/4\). For that index, \[f_i(z)-f_i(m_i)=\frac{\mu_i}{2}|z-m_i|^2\ge\frac{\beta R^2}{64}.\] The objective may depend on the algorithm's predetermined query, not on any randomized query or later feedback.

If the exact optimal value \(c=f(m)\) is known, let \(v=f(q)\) and \(g=f'(q)\). If \(g=0\), then \(q=m\) because \(\mu>0\). Otherwise \(v-c>0\) and \[\mu=\frac{g^2}{2(v-c)},\qquad m=q-\frac{g}{\mu}.\] Thus a single reply does recover the minimizer in that stronger information model, for this quadratic class. The two-instance lower bound does not grant the algorithm that additional scalar.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Strong
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Quadratic regularization at first-order regularity

Chewi arXiv2605.07006v1 Section4.1 Lemma4.2: the actual regularized objective
is strongly convex and smooth. No C² or Hessian hypothesis is introduced.
This component does not establish oracle complexity or the full reduction.
-/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticRegularizationFirstOrder
open Set InnerProductSpace
open scoped NNReal

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Quadratic regularization of a differentiable convex objective: actual
curvature, gradient and smoothness, including zero regularization. -/
theorem curvature_gradient_and_smoothness
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    {f : E → ℝ} (hd : Differentiable ℝ f) (hc : ConvexOn ℝ univ f)
    {β δ : ℝ≥0} (hL : LipschitzWith β (gradient f)) (u : E) :
    let W := fun x => f x + (δ : ℝ)/2*‖x-u‖^2
    Differentiable ℝ W ∧ StrongConvexOn univ (δ : ℝ) W ∧
      (∀ x, gradient W x = gradient f x + (δ : ℝ) • (x-u)) ∧
      LipschitzWith (β+δ) (gradient W) := by
  let W := fun x => f x + (δ : ℝ)/2*‖x-u‖^2
  have hq (x : E) : HasFDerivAt (fun z => (δ : ℝ)/2*‖z-u‖^2)
      ((δ : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ (x-u)) x := by
    convert (((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const u).norm_sq).const_mul ((δ : ℝ)/2)
      using 1 <;> first | rfl | (ext v; simp; ring)
  have hWd : Differentiable ℝ W := fun x => ((hd x).hasFDerivAt.add (hq x)).differentiableAt
  have hgrad (x : E) : gradient W x = gradient f x + (δ : ℝ) • (x-u) := by
    have hfd : fderiv ℝ W x = fderiv ℝ f x + (δ : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ (x-u) :=
      ((hd x).hasFDerivAt.add (hq x)).fderiv
    rw [gradient, hfd, map_add, map_smul]
    congr 1
    exact congrArg (fun v : E => (δ : ℝ) • v) ((toDual ℝ E).symm_apply_apply (x-u))
  have hstrong : StrongConvexOn univ (δ : ℝ) W := by
    apply strongConvexOn_iff_convex.mpr
    have ha := (hc.add (((-(δ : ℝ)) • (innerSL ℝ u).toLinearMap).convexOn convex_univ)).add_const
      ((δ : ℝ)/2*‖u‖^2)
    convert! ha using 1
    ext x
    simp [W, norm_sub_sq_real, real_inner_comm]
    ring
  refine ⟨hWd,hstrong,hgrad,?_⟩
  apply LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul
  intro x y
  rw [dist_eq_norm, hgrad, hgrad]
  have he : gradient f x + (δ : ℝ) • (x-u) -
      (gradient f y + (δ : ℝ) • (y-u)) =
      (gradient f x-gradient f y) + (δ : ℝ) • (x-y) := by
    simp only [smul_sub]
    abel
  rw [he]
  have hb := hL.dist_le_mul x y
  rw [dist_eq_norm, dist_eq_norm] at hb
  calc
    _ ≤ ‖gradient f x-gradient f y‖ + ‖(δ : ℝ) • (x-y)‖ := norm_add_le _ _
    _ ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖x-y‖ + (δ : ℝ)*‖x-y‖ := by
      rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg δ.coe_nonneg]
      linarith
    _ = ((β+δ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)*dist x y := by rw [dist_eq_norm]; simp; ring
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticRegularizationFirstOrder
